Most slide themes vary the typeface and leave the structure alone.

`comic` gives a deck the vocabulary of a comic book instead: cover and chapter splashes, single panels, action slides, speech bubbles, and halftone.
Each is a class on a heading or a div, so the source stays markdown and only the slides that want a visual take one.

[See a deck built by this site](preview.html).

![](preview.html){.embed-art loading="lazy" title="A deck in the comic format" style="--atelier-embed-art-ratio: 1.78;"}

## Starting a presentation

```bash
quarto use template {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

## Adding it to a presentation you already have

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

## Quick start

```yaml
format: comic-revealjs
```

Then opt a slide into a visual with a class on its heading:

```markdown
## Chapter 1: The Setup {.section}

## A Single Panel {.panel}

## {.action}

POW!
```

A slide with no class is an ordinary slide in the theme's styling.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every class, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for the source behind the deck.

## Where it works

RevealJS.
